title: Design Memory Allocator Free List
description:
Design a memory allocator `MemoryAllocator` managing a contiguous address space `[0, n - 1]` of size `n` (up to `10^9` units) using a **doubly linked list of memory segments** with free-block coalescing:
- `MemoryAllocator(int n)` initializes a single free segment `[0, n - 1]` of length `n`.
- `int allocate(int size, int mID)` finds the **leftmost** contiguous free block of length at least `size`, allocates its leftmost `size` units to memory ID `mID`, and returns the starting address. If no free block is large enough, returns `-1`.
- `int freeMemory(int mID)` frees all segments currently assigned to `mID`, coalescing each freed segment with any immediately adjacent free segments on its left or right, and returns the total number of units freed (`0` if `mID` owns no segments).
constraints: At most 1000 calls will be made to allocate and freeMemory.
hints: Because `n` can be as large as `10^9`, you cannot allocate an array of size `n`. Instead store segments `(start, length, mID)` (with `mID == 0` meaning free) in a doubly linked list and keep a map `mID -> list of owned nodes`.

On `allocate`, split the leftmost free node with `length >= size`; on `freeMemory(mID)`, mark each owned node free (`mID = 0`) and immediately merge it with `node.prev` and/or `node.next` whenever they are also free.

examples.explanation: Allocations fill indices 0,1,2; freeing mID 2 opens [1,1]; allocate(3,4) skips [1,1] to take [3..5]; freeing mID 1 frees 3 units across [0,1] and [6].
Works on a 10^9 address space: freeing the first 400M block lets a subsequent 300M allocation succeed at address 0.
Freeing mIDs 1, 3, then 2 coalesces all three regions back into a single 10-unit free block so allocate(10, 5) returns 0.
